Chapter 14. The Gift of Giving and the Joy of Service.
You know, there’s a special kind of happiness that comes from giving—whether that's your time, your attention, or just a little bit of care.
Service, in all its forms—big or small—does something powerful. It connects us to something bigger than just ourselves. And in that connection, we find meaning. We find purpose. And maybe most importantly, we find a sense of belonging.
I want you to picture a teenager, feeling totally isolated at school. She decides to volunteer at a local food bank—not because she’s seeking some big life change, but just to fill her afternoons.
At first, it’s routine. But slowly, as she gets to know the people she’s serving, something shifts. She starts to feel real connection—and pride. She realizes that giving her time and attention brings her more happiness than anything she’s ever done just for herself.
Most of the time, people don’t even notice how much joy is hiding in service. We’re told happiness comes from what we get, right? But time and again, the deepest, most lasting satisfaction actually comes from what we give.
Think about a retiree who once focused only on his own comfort—his own little world. After stepping up to mentor young people, he discovers brand new purpose. The friendships he builds turn into a huge source of energy and joy.
What’s amazing is, service isn’t really a sacrifice. It’s a gift—not just for others, but for ourselves too.
So many people struggling with unhappiness are actually wrestling with isolation or just feeling like their lives lack meaning.
And here’s the thing. Giving doesn’t have to be some grand gesture. Sometimes, it’s as simple as listening, offering a helping hand, or saying a few encouraging words.
When service becomes a part of your daily life, happiness naturally grows. It takes root in the connections you make and the generosity you share.
So, next time you’re searching for joy, maybe ask yourself—how can I give a little more today?
